clue.text: A small amount of dessert

definitions.meaning: a trifling quantity, a mere bit of something
the layered pudding of sponge, custard, fruit and cream

explanation.surface: A diner asks for just a little helping of pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a tiny quantity and a classic British layered pudding of sponge, jelly, custard and cream.

clue.text: Negotiate with skill to mount new production of Cats

indicators.note: to mount in a down clue means the word for skill climbs upward, so it reads backwards

parts.note: art means skill

indicators.note: a new production of a show rearranges it, so the word Cats is shuffled

explanation.surface: A theatre producer negotiates skilfully to stage a revival of the musical Cats.
explanation.definitionFit: To conduct and carry through business such as a deal is to negotiate it, a close synonym.

clue.text: Consequently Len gets a bit of teasing after wearing lippy

indicators.note: after places the following pieces behind the word for wearing

parts.note: wearing means in, as in dressed in
so means consequently or therefore
taken as written

indicators.note: a bit of picks out just the opening letter of the word teasing

explanation.surface: Len gets teased as a result of wearing lipstick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lippy' looks like British slang for lipstick; here it is the adjective meaning cheeky.
explanation.definitionFit: Lippy is informal British for cheeky or impertinent, a synonym for rudely disrespectful.

clue.text: Proceed with difficulty when lacking energy

definitions.meaning: to hobble along with an injured leg

explanation.surface: Struggling forward when tired out.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to walk lamely and the adjective means floppy or weak, two senses of one word.

clue.text: Father's spoken about Tasso's earliest poetic style

indicators.note: about means the father's and spoken pieces go around the letter picked from Tasso

parts.note: Pa is a familiar word for father, so father's gives PAS
spoken means oral, said rather than written

indicators.note: earliest signals taking the first letter of the poet's name Tasso

explanation.surface: A priest's lecture on the early poetic manner of Torquato Tasso.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Father's spoken' tempts you toward a homophone, but 'spoken' simply means ORAL. Tasso was an Italian Renaissance poet who wrote a pastoral drama, Aminta.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes verse idealising rural shepherd life, a recognised genre of poetry.

clue.text: Essential for every man to consume drink during it

parts.note: all means every one

indicators.note: during means everything before it goes inside the word it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to consume means the man swallows the drink, so the drink sits inside

parts.note: taken as written
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: It's vital that every man has a drink throughout the occasion.
explanation.definitionFit: Something of the utmost significance is crucial or vital, so the phrase means essential.

clue.text: Try at first taking sheep by public transport

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of the word Try

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: Try taking a sheep along on the bus.
explanation.definitionFit: A streetcar running on rails in the road is a kind of public transport.

clue.text: Consider following soldiers to get back

indicators.note: following places the word for consider after the soldiers

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, British army soldiers
to deem is to consider or judge

explanation.surface: Think about trailing behind the troops in order to return.
explanation.definitionFit: To redeem a pawned item or coupon is to recover it by payment, so it means get back.

clue.text: Fat queen found in pantry

parts.note: lard is pig fat used in cooking
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A greasy queen discovered hiding in a food store.
explanation.definitionFit: A cool room or cupboard for storing food is a synonym for pantry.

clue.text: Dancing amuses when appropriate

indicators.note: letters that are dancing move about, so the word amuses is rearranged

explanation.surface: A performance is entertaining whenever the occasion suits it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appropriate' reads as an adjective in the surface, but it is the verb meaning to take for oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: To appropriate power or a title is to take it over, a synonym in the sense of seizing.

clue.text: Working alone at the German plant

indicators.note: working letters are set in motion and rearranged, so alone is shuffled

parts.note: der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: Someone toils alone at a German factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' in the surface suggests a factory; it is a shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a poisonous evergreen flowering shrub of the Mediterranean, an example of a plant.

clue.text: Dresses and stockings worn by Russia's top fashion model

parts.note: dresses are items of clothes

indicators.note: worn by means the stockings go on around the letter from Russia

parts.note: hose is a word for stockings or tights

indicators.note: top picks the first letter of Russia in a down clue

explanation.surface: A top Russian model wears dresses and stockings on the catwalk.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is jokey: the frame used for drying laundry, and slang for someone who loves showing off clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally someone who wears clothes beautifully and lives for fashion, likened to a drying rack draped in garments.

clue.text: Shelf stacker's first to get sick

indicators.note: first here means only the opening letter of the word stacker is used

parts.note: sick means ill

explanation.surface: A supermarket shelf stacker is the first employee to fall ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shelf stacker' reads as one phrase, but the definition is just 'Shelf'.
explanation.definitionFit: A window ledge is a narrow shelf of stone or wood at the base of the window opening.

clue.text: Full page on growth

parts.note: a lump is a swelling or growth on the body

explanation.surface: A whole page given over to an article about a tumour.
explanation.definitionFit: Full and rounded in shape, as in a well-filled figure or cushion, a synonym.

clue.text: Measure piece of tubing removed from lake

indicators.note: removed from says that letter is taken out of the measure

parts.note: a metre is a measure of length

indicators.note: a piece of here is just the opening letter of the word tubing

explanation.surface: Someone measures a length of pipe pulled out of a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A poetic or regional word for a lake or pond, as in Windermere and other English place names.

clue.text: Depend on receiving Penny's answer

indicators.note: receiving means the word for depend takes in the penny abbreviation

parts.note: to rely on someone is to depend on them
P is the abbreviation for a penny

explanation.surface: Count on getting Penny's response.
explanation.definitionFit: A reply is a response given back, a direct synonym.

clue.text: A round clasp

definitions.meaning: a musical round, a song for voices entering in turn, often comic
a fastening device such as on a door or bag

explanation.surface: A circular fastener.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a type of comic round sung in parts and a fastening device or clasp.

clue.text: Customary for a religious community on this island at the start of Lent

parts.note: a convent is a community of nuns
Iona is the Hebridean island where Columba founded his monastery, fitting the religious theme

indicators.note: at the start of signals the opening letter of the word Lent

explanation.surface: Fasting at the start of Lent is usual for monks and nuns on a holy island.
explanation.walkthrough: IONA is a small island off western Scotland, famous for its early abbey.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done according to accepted convention is customary, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Heads of British industry look with amazement around Poland's financial centre

indicators.note: heads of picks out the first letters of British and industry
around means the gaping word goes round Poland's code

parts.note: to gape is to stare in wonder
PL is the international vehicle code for Poland

explanation.surface: British business chiefs stare in awe at Warsaw's financial district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poland's financial centre' looks like the definition, but Poland only gives PL.
explanation.definitionFit: New York City, nicknamed this, is home to Wall Street and the world's leading financial centre.

clue.text: Protective layer for example seen on German racing boat

parts.note: a shell is a light narrow racing boat used in rowing

explanation.surface: A protective coat, for instance, is seen on a German rowing boat.
explanation.definitionFit: The thin hard covering of an egg is a protective layer for the yolk and white.

clue.text: Hannah More for example is a Conservative with shares in Google primarily

parts.note: blue is the colour of the UK Conservative Party, so a Tory is a blue
stock means shares in a company
taken as written

indicators.note: primarily picks out the first letter of the word Google

explanation.surface: A writer is described as a Tory investor in a tech giant.
explanation.walkthrough: Hannah More was an 18th-century English writer and member of the learned women's circle whose name gave rise to the label.
explanation.definitionFit: The term means an intellectual or literary woman, and Hannah More is a celebrated historic example.

clue.text: What John Shakespeare was extremely genteel about

indicators.note: extremely means the two outermost letters of genteel are kept

parts.note: over means about, as in quarrelling over something

explanation.surface: John Shakespeare was famously very refined about his work.
explanation.walkthrough: John Shakespeare, the playwright's father, was a glove-maker in Stratford-upon-Avon.
explanation.definitionFit: William Shakespeare's father made and sold gloves, so the trade name describes his occupation.

clue.text: Bottle shown by mother to grab unruly nag

indicators.note: to grab means mother holds the shuffled horse inside her

parts.note: mum is a British word for mother

indicators.note: unruly means the letters of nag are disordered

explanation.surface: A mother seizes a wild horse and displays a big bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: A large wine bottle holding twice the standard amount, so it is one type of bottle.

clue.text: Gain knowledge mostly from this poet

indicators.note: mostly signals that the word for gaining knowledge loses its final letter

parts.note: to learn is to gain knowledge

explanation.surface: Readers can learn a great deal from studying this poet.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward Lear was the Victorian writer of nonsense verse and limericks.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Lear, author of The Owl and the Pussy-cat, is the poet the clue points at by name-play.

clue.text: James Hunt's showing what he was trying to avoid

definitions.text: what he was trying to avoid

indicators.note: showing says the letters are on display within the racing driver's name

explanation.surface: Formula One champion James Hunt reveals what he was always trying to steer clear of.
explanation.walkthrough: In motor-racing slang a shunt is a crash, exactly what a racing driver like Hunt wants to avoid; the definition is fair because it refers back to the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A racing slang term for a collision between cars, which every driver tries to avoid.

clue.text: Free ticket's almost out of date

indicators.note: almost means the word for out of date loses its last letter

parts.note: passe means old-fashioned or out of date

explanation.surface: A complimentary ticket has nearly expired.
explanation.definitionFit: A pass is a ticket or permit granting free admission or travel.

clue.text: Change colour when shot

definitions.meaning: as leaves do in autumn, or milk going off
a go or attempt, one's chance in order

explanation.surface: Changing colour after being shot.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaves change colour in autumn, and a go or attempt in a sequence is also called by this word.

clue.text: Edges away from Cromwell perhaps to escape death

indicators.note: edges away from means the outer letters of the name are dropped

parts.note: Oliver Cromwell was Lord Protector; perhaps signals the first name stands for any Oliver

explanation.surface: Someone sidles away from Cromwell to avoid execution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Edges away' reads as a verb of moving off, but it means the ends are removed.
explanation.definitionFit: To survive and go on existing is to stay alive, the opposite of dying.

clue.text: Tsar not initially having a person keeping watch in front

indicators.note: not initially means the tsar's name drops its first letter

parts.note: Ivan was the name of several Russian tsars, including Ivan the Terrible
a guard is a person on watch

explanation.surface: A Russian emperor has a sentry posted ahead of him.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the phrase 'in front', used as a noun position: the leading part of an army or movement.
explanation.definitionFit: The leading section of an advancing force is the part at the front, so the phrase describes it.

clue.text: The wife of Bath had one trick to ensnare a politician

definitions.text: The wife of Bath had one

indicators.note: to ensnare means the trick closes around the politician

parts.note: a wile is a cunning trick
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Chaucer's Wife of Bath used a ruse to snare a member of parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wife of Bath is a pilgrim in Chaucer's Canterbury Tales, described wearing an elaborate wimple-style headdress.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval woman's linen head covering framing the face, the kind of garment Chaucer's pilgrim wore.

clue.text: Memo's about getting a bodyguard

parts.note: re is a Latin-derived word meaning about or concerning
a minder is a bodyguard

explanation.surface: A memorandum concerning the hiring of a personal bodyguard.
explanation.definitionFit: A memo is a short note to jog the memory, so it is a prompt of that kind.

clue.text: Show girl captured by artist at end of rehearsal

indicators.note: captured by means the girl's name sits inside the artist

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword staple for artist
Eve is a girl's name

indicators.note: at end of picks out the last letter of the word rehearsal

explanation.surface: A showgirl is caught by a painter at the close of a rehearsal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Show girl' reads as one showbiz noun; the definition is just 'Show'.
